title: Executive Landscape

sections.heading: 1. How modern C4ISR is structured: the chain and the layers
paragraphs: Modern U.S. C4ISR is best read as a fifteen-step information and decision chain rather than a list of programs: COLLECT, TRANSPORT, INGEST, NORMALIZE, STORE, PROCESS, FUSE, IDENTIFY, VISUALIZE, DECIDE, COLLABORATE, DISSEMINATE, TASK, MONITOR and ASSESS. Every seam between steps is a format translation (Link 16 J-series, VMF, USMTF, CoT/TAK protobuf, STANAG 4607/4609/4676, NITF, MIL-STD-2525), a security-domain crossing or a human control point, and the documented pain sits at those seams rather than inside the steps (FACT for the architecture assembled in the S00 chain map from Army, Air Force, GAO and public SDK/protocol sources; HIGH).

The chain resolves into seven layers. Sensors and transport are hardware- and waveform-heavy and belong to primes, SpaceX and government radio programs. Above them sits a newly commercial two-tier data layer: Anduril Lattice (tactical) and Palantir Foundry (cloud) with Raft for registries and federation, declared the NGC2 common data layer baseline on June 22, 2026 (FACT, HIGH), and Palantir's Maven Smart System as the joint equivalent run by NGA and CDAO across three security domains with 20,000-plus users (NGA, 2025; FACT, HIGH on stated counts). Processing splits into two grades: fire-control-quality fusion (Northrop IBCS in full-rate production since November 2025, Aegis, Link 16 track management) is closed, safety-certified and prime-owned, while situational-awareness fusion (Lattice entity merge, Foundry ontology, TAK Server) is the commercially contested world. Applications sit on top: planning (Onebrief, Microsoft), warfighting-function apps (fires, airspace, sustainment), autonomy C2 and the COP (ATAK/WinTAK, Lattice UI, Foundry apps, GCCS-J legacy, SitaWare and HexaForce abroad). Two cross-cutting security layers, cross-domain solutions with data-centric labeling and ICAM/zero trust/continuous ATO, gate everything that crosses a classification or national boundary (FACT, HIGH).

Three structural facts follow. The government-owned TAK/CoT ecosystem (500,000-plus users; TAK Server and TAK Protocol v1 on GitHub) has commoditized the basic COP client, so a new COP is not a product (FACT, HIGH). The human control points are fixed by policy: positive identification and target approval are human, releasability is decided by foreign disclosure officers, and authorizing officials personally accept ATO risk (FACT, HIGH). ASSESS is the weakest step: GAO found in April 2025 that DoD still had no framework to guide CJADC2 investments or measure progress, that services build C2 'largely in isolation', and that overly restrictive classification is a 'significant hindrance' to sharing with no DoD entity owning the fix (GAO-25-106454, 2025-04-08; FACT, HIGH).
sections.label_notes: Chain and layer descriptions are FACT/HIGH where they cite named programs, published SDKs or protocol specifications; mapping specific products to chain steps is INFERENCE/MEDIUM where contract values are undisclosed. Vendor sensor-to-shooter timings (sub-one-minute fire missions at Ivy Sting) are HYPOTHESIS: no independent exercise measurement was found.

sections.heading: 2. Where value is moving, with evidence
paragraphs: The defining shift of 2024-2026 is from monolithic programs of record (CPCE, DCGS-A, the AFATDS-era fires chain) to commercially owned data platforms with third-party app ecosystems, and money is following. NGC2 became an Army program of record in 2025, awarded prototype OTAs to Team Anduril (about $99.6M, July 2025) and a Lockheed Martin team (about $26M, September 2025), ran a serialized campaign (Ivy Sting 1-5, Ivy Mass, Lightning Surge 1-3, Operation Jailbreak in May 2026, Project Convergence Capstone 6 in July 2026), declared the Lattice/Foundry/Raft baseline in June 2026 and was called 'ready to scale' in August 2026 (army.mil, 2026-08-03; FACT, HIGH). GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20) confirms scale and risk: about $3.3B identified through FY2026, a tentative goal of 11 divisions and four corps by FY2032, but no life-cycle cost estimate and no unit-by-year schedule (FACT, HIGH). The FY2027 request is roughly $3.78B across applications, data, infrastructure and transport, while the FY26 NDAA capped NGC2 obligations at 50 percent pending a report and the HASC FY27 mark cut $710M (E05 comptroller sweep; FACT, MEDIUM on exact figures).

At the joint level Maven Smart System has become the de facto developer platform: its IDIQ ceiling rose from $480M (May 2024) to about $1.3B through 2029 (DefenseScoop, 2025-05-23; FACT, HIGH; ceiling, not revenue); the Deputy Secretary's April 2026 directive made AI-enabled decision-making 'the cornerstone' of CJADC2 with an 'aggressive' component transition timeline (DefenseScoop, 2026-04-03 and 2026-04-15; FACT, HIGH); Maven was designated a program of record in 2026 (month reported inconsistently; MEDIUM); and the FY2027 request seeks more than $2B in FY27 and about $2.3B across the FYDP for Maven plus the Joint Fires Network, explicitly to move 'from fragmented deployments to Joint enterprise tooling' (DefenseScoop, 2026-05-28; FACT, HIGH). Open DAGIR, CDAO's May 2024 government-owned-interface initiative for third-party apps, is the formal counterweight to lock-in, but its 2026 status is unverified (public evidence insufficient), and CDAO's enterprise data layer is unstable: the 2026 DoD IG Advana audit saw 10 of 12 recommendations rejected and the recompete was cancelled and split into a War Data Platform (E01; FACT, MEDIUM).

The Department of the Air Force converged on the same pattern a year later: PAE C3BM (renamed from PEO in January 2026) owns the DAF Battle Network; the ABMS RDT&E request was $1,040.5M in FY26 with Cloud-Based C2 inside it; SciTec (Firefly Aerospace) was selected as CBC2 data fusion provider in Q2 2026; DASH sprints at ShOC-N validate industry software and transition it to classified networks (af.mil, 2026-09-08; FACT, HIGH). Navy Project Overmatch is fielded to three carrier strike groups (C4ISRNET, 2024-03-06) but its unclassified core line was only $139.8M in FY25 with most funding classified (E05; FACT, MEDIUM), making the Navy the least observable buyer. Space Force transport is SpaceX-anchored: a $2.29B MILNET award in May 2026 and SDA Tranche 1 Transport at 63 of 126 satellites by July 16, 2026 after a months-long pause (SpaceNews; FACT, HIGH).

Value is also moving down and sideways. Downward into DDIL synchronization and edge integration: Ivy Mass demonstrated local tracking with later synchronization under degraded comms, PC-C6 still reported intermittent connectivity and overheating gear, CDAO funded an approximately $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA to Anduril (December 2024), Ditto is under USMC Project Dynamis evaluation, Defense Unicorns raised $136M (January 2026) and Anduril acquired Klas (FACT, MEDIUM-HIGH). Sideways into data-centric security and releasability, which GAO, the DoD CIO zero-trust office and exercise reporting all name as the binding constraint on coalition and cross-domain sharing (FACT, HIGH on the pain; INFERENCE on thin supply). And into autonomy C2, a demonstrated failure point pulling money: Replicator delivered 'hundreds' rather than thousands of systems by August 2025, partly because software could not command large heterogeneous drone sets (CRS via secondary; FACT, MEDIUM); DIU issued C2/ACT prototype awards to seven companies (November 2024); Replicator was folded into the DAWG in late 2025; and the FY2027 DAWG request is reported at $54.6B alongside a 200,000-drone 'Drone Dominance' target (S13; FACT, MEDIUM).
sections.label_notes: Dollar figures are labeled ceiling vs request vs obligation; none of the ceilings ($20B Anduril Army enterprise agreement, $10B Palantir Army EA, $1.3B Maven, $13B pLEO IDIQ) is revenue. The Maven program-of-record month and the FY27 DAWG figure are MEDIUM because sources disagree or could not be read at primary level.

sections.heading: 3. Which layers are crowded (and by whom)
paragraphs: Five layers are crowded to the point where a new entrant needs a reason to exist beyond being newer. (a) COP, visualization and geospatial SA: the government-owned TAK family, Lattice UI, Foundry and Maven apps, Lockheed CommandIQ, Systematic SitaWare and Thales HexaForce in NATO markets, with Booz Allen (via PAR Government) as the dominant TAK services house at services-priced economics (FACT, HIGH). (b) Core data platform and middleware: Foundry, Lattice, Raft, Striveworks, Govini and every prime's integration platform; the Army has chosen, and the S02 sweep found no price point for standalone middleware between 'free government standard' and 'bundled by Anduril/Palantir' (INFERENCE, HIGH). (c) Autonomy and swarm C2: Anduril Lattice (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM $86M, CCA), Shield AI, Auterion ($130M Series B), Swarm Aero, the L3Harris-led ACT team, Tesseract, XTEND and Quantum, with government reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA, STANAG 4586) commoditizing the layer further (FACT, HIGH). (d) Counter-UAS C2: Parsons DroneArmor, Anduril's Army counter-drone fire-control selection (October 2025), Hidden Level ($100M OTA) and many others (FACT, MEDIUM-HIGH). (e) Fire-control C2: IBCS, Aegis, CEC and FAAD C2, closed and safety-certified (FACT, HIGH).

Three adjacent layers are held by well-capitalized specialists who can absorb features: accredited hosting and DevSecOps (Platform One, free to programs; Second Front; Defense Unicorns; Palantir FedStart/Apollo; hyperscalers under JWCC), enterprise zero trust and ICAM (Booz Allen Thunderdome, Microsoft) with cross-domain solutions an NSA-assessed oligopoly (Everfox, Owl, General Dynamics Mission Systems, Northrop, Lockheed), and tactical transport software (Anduril, Aalyria, Persistent Systems, Motorola/Silvus, RII/CodeMettle). In each case the segment sweeps concluded that a missing competitor in a sub-niche reflects incumbents' priorities rather than open demand (INFERENCE, HIGH).
sections.label_notes: Company positioning is FACT where a government award or public product is cited and INFERENCE where the study judged a product 'absorbable'. NGC2 team-member participation is vendor-stated; member contract values are undisclosed.

sections.heading: 4. Which layers remain fragmented, and why fragmentation is not opportunity
paragraphs: The chain map and evidence sweeps converge on seven fragmented layers: DDIL synchronization and edge replication (Ditto plus a few named vendors, while Ivy Sting 4-5 still had industry 'fixing the code in almost real time', DVIDS 2026-03-30; FACT, HIGH); data-centric security, labeling and releasability (the DoD CIO zero-trust office described tagging as 'phone calls, IERs, weeks of negotiation' in September 2025; WFX 24-03 intelligence had to be regenerated on the MPE enclave with REL NATO markings, MIPB 2025; Balikatan 2026's first eight-nation COP took 'more than eight years' and still depends on foreign-disclosure officers; FACT, HIGH); assessment, BDA and effects analytics (no named systems or incumbents found; not evidence of demand); tactical-edge sustainment data (Air and Rune the only named entrants; EBS-C regressed in 2026; FACT, MEDIUM); electromagnetic battle management (public evidence insufficient); test, instrumentation and C2 experimentation tooling (Operation Jailbreak needed about 600 people from 55-80 firms to expose interfaces, DefenseScoop 2026-05-29; FACT, HIGH); and legacy message-format translation (SBIR-funded translators failing to transition for roughly twenty years, E04; FACT, MEDIUM).

The study red-teamed all 36 consolidated gaps in these layers and killed 35. The kill reasons repeat: the buyer chain breaks at program office, budget line or vehicle (the government performs the function itself, as with test and conformance in C5ISR Center's Radio Rodeo and ATEC labs, or has never funded it, as with coalition releasability tooling, demonstrated since 2022 with no program of record); the platform owner can absorb the feature (Anduril, Palantir, Raft, Ditto, TAK Product Center, IS4S in PNT); and nationality, clearance and export gates fall exactly where the value is (classified marking guides, Secret-REL enclaves, USML-controlled EW and fire-control interfaces). Policy, not technology, binds sharing, as both GAO and an AFA 2026 panelist stated ('not actually a technological impediment... policy impediments', af.mil, 2026-09-21; FACT, HIGH). Fragmentation here is fragmentation of buyers and authorities, not an unserved market (INFERENCE, HIGH).
sections.label_notes: Pain evidence is FACT/HIGH where it comes from GAO, Army journals, DVIDS or DoD CIO webinars; several sam.gov RFI pointers are FACT on existence but their text was not read directly (egress-blocked). The conclusion that fragmentation is not opportunity is INFERENCE built on 36 gap red teams.

sections.heading: 5. Major procurement trends, 2024-2026
paragraphs: OTAs and Commercial Solutions Openings are now the default front door. NGC2 was competed through a CSO with rolling windows; the Air Force JADC2 CSO (FA8612-21-S-C001) is open to November 9, 2026; Space Force's Kronos family awarded sub-$1M prototype OTs to small vendors in 2026; DIU remains the main OSD route, reporting a 51 percent prototype-to-production transition rate for FY2016-2023, where 'transition' means any production contract, not scaled fielding (GAO-25-106856; FACT, HIGH). The March 2025 software-acquisition memo made the Software Acquisition Pathway preferred and CSO/OTA the default, and the November 7, 2025 'Warfighting Acquisition System' memo replaces PEOs with Portfolio Acquisition Executives within two years under a commercial-first policy (media.defense.gov, 2025-11-10; DefenseScoop, 2025-11-07; FACT, HIGH). For this team the decisive fact is that Other Transactions carry no statutory ownership test, unlike SBIR (E07; FACT, HIGH).

Authorization reform is real but unfinished. The February 2022 continuous-ATO memo, the April 24, 2025 Software Fast Track (SWFT) memo and its RFIs (more than 400 responses), the September 2025 Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct and FedRAMP 20x all push toward automated, SBOM-based, continuous intake; vendor-side reporting says SWFT moved from pilot to expected requirement in January 2026 (secondary blogs; MEDIUM-LOW). Yet DoD CIO's 2025 DevSecOps study records authorizing officials 'biased to caution', an Army CTO memo in September 2025 rated the NGC2 prototype 'very high risk' for lacking access control, logging and app vetting (secondary; MEDIUM), and CMMC's DFARS clause took effect November 10, 2025 while the Phase 2 third-party transition was suspended in July 2026 (E07; FACT, MEDIUM). Every prior fix has been a policy change and policy is still moving (INFERENCE, HIGH).

Consolidation and new entry are happening at once, at different layers. Consolidation: Anduril's ten-year Army enterprise agreement with a $20B ceiling (June 2026), Palantir's $10B-ceiling Army EA (July 2025), Maven's directed transition, the NGC2 data-layer decision and M&A (Anduril-Klas, Booz Allen-PAR, Motorola-Silvus, Firefly-SciTec). New entry: Onebrief (reported at a $2B-plus valuation with an Army enterprise contract in September 2026; MEDIUM), Air, Striveworks, Govini, Rune, Ditto and Defense Unicorns all won NGC2-adjacent slots, almost always as members of a prime- or Anduril-led team with undisclosed values, entered through exercise self-teaming rather than solicitations (E03; FACT on participation, HIGH). Primes persist: Lockheed leads the 25th ID stack, Northrop holds IBCS ($1.4B LRIP/FRP), L3Harris leads the Replicator C2 team, SAIC holds the Joint Fires Network, and Data Link Solutions took a $248M Navy MIDS JTRS order in January 2026 (FACT, HIGH). Record private funding ($49.1B raised by defense-tech startups in 2025) is capital supply, not demand (E04; FACT, HIGH).

Budget lines are concentrating into a few flexible pots: NGC2 (about $3.78B FY27 request), Maven/JFN (more than $2B FY27), ABMS/DAF Battle Network ($1,040.5M FY26), CANES ($534.3M FY26) and Space Force 'Automate Sat C2' ($1.5B new), while legacy lines (ITN, CPCE/Mission Command, C2 Fix) are divested or folded in; the 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) has no discrete C2-software line (E05; FACT, MEDIUM-HIGH). Countervailing facts: Congress is pushing back on flexible funding (the 50 percent NGC2 cap, the $710M HASC cut), GAO's 2026 annual assessment puts average capability delivery above 12 years while acquisition staffing shrank in 2025 (E01; FACT, HIGH), and SBIR/STTR authority lapsed on September 30, 2025 before restoration by S. 3971 on April 13, 2026 with the 13 CFR 121.702 ownership test unchanged (E07; FACT, HIGH).
sections.label_notes: Policy memos and NDAA provisions are FACT/HIGH from primary or reputable secondary sources retrieved this session (GAO-26-108019, media.defense.gov WAS memo, DefenseScoop). SWFT's January 2026 'requirement' status is MEDIUM-LOW (vendor blogs only). Line-item figures come from the E05 comptroller sweep and were not all re-read at PE level.

sections.heading: 6. Primary conclusion for these two founders: what to pursue, what to avoid, and why
paragraphs: The honest headline is that the study did not find a venture-scale opening in U.S. C4ISR software that these founders can attack in 2026 with $250k. Of 36 gaps, one survived as borderline and only narrowed: G04, a vendor-neutral composite-assurance engine for assured PNT (an ASPN 2023/pntOS-C-conformant service producing per-source health, composite confidence, explainable jam/spoof/fault classification and a fallback recommendation), scored 2.5 on market attractiveness and 3.3 on founder fit, MEDIUM confidence. Its case: a program of record (NAVWAR GPNTS) published a software-only topic (DON26BX05-NP004), named itself transition owner, accepted synthetic open-standard data and planned multiple Phase I awards; ASPN 2023 and the pntOS C API went public in 2026, removing the proprietary-interface barrier of GAO-21-320SP; and GPS denial is routine (12 DoD interference tests in August-September 2026). Its weaknesses: the only evidenced vehicle closed September 23, 2026; no program budget line for awareness software exists (DoD funded pntOS integration at $17M against $783M of PNT S&T in FY20-24); IS4S authored the standards and holds an Army NorthStar OTA of up to $41M (April 2026); and the SBIR ownership test collides with the cap table. The recommended pursuit is narrow: spend roughly $100k-$150k over four to five months on the engine rather than a dashboard, take it to NP004 Phase I awardees and the GPNTS integrator as a subcontract component, to OT/CSO doors with no ownership test (IWRP, NavalX/ANTX, DIU), and to an unclassified civil or allied maritime operator as a first paying beachhead; abandon it if a PNT-integrity engineer and a former Navy watchstander cannot be recruited within six months (INFERENCE from the G04 scorecard; MEDIUM).

Two killed gaps remain useful as paths, not companies. G29, an open-source 'TAK DDIL bench' (containerized ATAK-CIV and TAK Server nodes behind emulated links, a sync scorer, API contract tests and a plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module), is buildable for $30k-$60k in three to four months, is unclassified by construction, is plausibly legal for the non-U.S.-person founder to build (counsel to confirm), and is the best-evidenced way to earn relationships with Jailbreak-series vendors, C5ISR Center's NetModX/Radio Rodeo and an NGC2 team lead's T&E cell; it was killed as a venture because the government owns and resources the function and platform owners give the test environment away (HIGH). G34, offline-first ICS/orders/LOGSTAT objects with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV sold to public-safety incident command, is the best bootstrappable fallback (founder fit 3.8; no SBIR, CUI or ATO) but abandons the U.S. defense goal and competes with free TAK Data Sync, Ditto and mature incident-management vendors with no moat (MEDIUM). The recommended sequence: (0) counsel-led structuring of cap table, export classification and a technology control plan before any code that touches controlled data; (1) build the G29 bench and one TAK-CIV integration as public credibility assets; (2) use them to enter an NGC2 team member's or TAK plugin shop's orbit and a NetModX or xTech slot; (3) run the G04 engine as the single product bet with civil/allied maritime as the revenue hedge; (4) re-evaluate at 12-18 months against section 8, including whether an EU/NATO-domiciled entity (DIANA's 24-month rapid-adoption path, Germany's D-LBO, the UK Digital Targeting Web) gives the German founder a structurally larger market than a U.S.-domiciled ITAR-exposed product (E06; INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Avoid: a new data fabric, middleware or platform (the Army and joint decisions are made; no price point exists); a new COP client or generic TAK plugin business (commoditized, services-priced); autonomy orchestration or a common controller (Anduril, Shield AI, Auterion plus government reference architectures; fifteen years of common-controller purgatory); cross-domain solutions, CSfC or enterprise ICAM (NSA-assessed oligopoly, sole-source follow-ons); sensors, radios, satellites or edge hardware (capital-intensive, ITAR-adjacent, consolidating); anything specially designed for fire control, EW/direction finding, military UAS control, SIGINT PED or targeting (USML or 600-series drift, deemed-export licensing for the Indonesian founder, clearances that require citizenship and are five-plus years away for both founders); and DISA/JWCC, DARPA or SBIR-first strategies for first revenue. The recurring reason is the same buyer-chain break: prototype awards, ceilings and exercise slots are not revenue, and every fragmented layer in section 4 is fragmented at the level of authorities and budgets that two students cannot change (INFERENCE, HIGH).
sections.label_notes: Recommendations are INFERENCE built on the gap scorecards and buyer maps; confidence is MEDIUM for G04, HIGH for the kills of G29 and G34 as ventures, and MEDIUM for the EU/NATO domicile alternative. Nothing here is a legal determination on SBIR eligibility, ITAR/EAR classification, FOCI or immigration; each requires specialist counsel.

sections.heading: 7. Research saturation
paragraphs: The study ran fifteen segment deep dives, five buyer maps, seven evidence sweeps, fourteen company records and a 71-candidate to 36-entry gap registry with full red teams, using WebSearch (capped in every stage), Bigdata.com full-text indexes and GitHub mirrors, with WebFetch to .gov, .mil and most news domains egress-blocked throughout; this session added four targeted web checks (GAO-26-108019, the WAS memo, the FY27 Maven/JFN request, SWFT status). Coverage is strong for NGC2, Maven, TITAN, IBCS, the DAF Battle Network, SDA transport, Replicator/DAWG, PC-C6, the TAK/CoT/Lattice data models, acquisition reform and the founders' regulatory position, and thin or absent for Overmatch specifics, the fires chain, GCCS-J/JPES, the DCGS family, cross-domain procurement, EMBM, tactical logistics C2, the texts of the April 2026 Maven directive and the September 2025 NGC2 security memo, DODIG-2025-126 findings, PE-level lines for a dozen programs, any MPE/coalition RFI, and any independent sensor-to-shooter measurement. The saturation_statement field carries the full account.
sections.label_notes: FACT description of the study's own method and limits; 'strong' versus 'thin' coverage is the analysts' INFERENCE.

sections.heading: 8. Top uncertainties for further research
paragraphs: The ten uncertainties that would most change this conclusion are listed in the top_uncertainties field. The three with highest leverage for these founders are whether NAVWAR re-issues NP004 or a Direct-to-Phase-II and who the Phase I awardees are (expected around Q1 2027); whether counsel can construct a compliant cap table and export classification that lets the Indonesian founder work on core code; and whether Open DAGIR and the Maven program-of-record transition ever publish third-party onboarding terms, data rights and revenue for small vendors.
sections.label_notes: All items are open questions (HYPOTHESIS by definition); the NP004 award timing is INFERENCE from the Navy's published cycle.

primary_conclusion: Modern C4ISR has re-formed around commercially owned data platforms (Anduril Lattice and Palantir Foundry for the Army since June 2026, Palantir Maven at the joint level, PAE C3BM's DAF Battle Network, a largely classified Navy Overmatch) with app ecosystems on top, and 2024-2026 procurement has shifted to OTAs, CSOs, the software pathway, SWFT-style continuous authorization and a commercial-first 'Warfighting Acquisition System'; money is concentrating into a few flexible pots (NGC2 about $3.78B FY27 request, Maven/JFN more than $2B) while Congress caps and cuts them. For these two founders the study did not find a venture-scale opening: of 36 red-teamed gaps, 35 died on the same three facts (the buyer chain breaks at program office, budget line or vehicle; the platform owner or a government lab can absorb the feature; and nationality, clearance and export-control gates fall exactly where the value is). The one borderline survivor is a narrow, vendor-neutral assured-PNT composite-assurance engine (G04) pursued as a subcontract component to NAVWAR NP004 awardees, through OT/CSO doors that carry no ownership test, and into an unclassified civil/allied maritime beachhead, contingent on recruiting a PNT-integrity engineer and a former Navy watchstander within six months. The recommended sequence is counsel-led structuring first, then a sub-$60k open-source TAK DDIL conformance bench (G29) as a credibility asset, then the G04 engine as the single product bet, with an EU/NATO-domiciled entity as an explicit alternative for the German founder; avoid platforms, COP clients, autonomy orchestration, CDS/ICAM, hardware and anything specially designed for fire control, EW, targeting or military UAS control. Confidence: HIGH on the landscape and the kills, MEDIUM on the G04 path.
top_uncertainties: Whether NAVWAR re-issues topic NP004 (closed 2026-09-23) or offers a Direct-to-Phase-II, and who the Phase I awardees are (expected around Q1 2027); the G04 path depends on subcontracting to them or to the GPNTS integrator.

Whether a SBIR-compliant cap table is achievable for this team under 13 CFR 121.702 and AFWERX foreign-national work rules, and on what timeline the German founder's permanent residence is granted; requires counsel, not analyst judgment.

The export classification (EAR99/5D002 vs USML or 600-series) of a generic PNT-assurance engine or DDIL-test harness, which determines whether the Indonesian founder can work on core code and whether a technology control plan suffices.

Whether Open DAGIR and the 2026 Maven program-of-record transition publish third-party app onboarding terms, data rights and revenue-sharing for small vendors; nothing public exists today, and the program-of-record month itself is reported inconsistently.

Whether NGC2 scales past two divisions on the FY27 request after the 50 percent obligation cap and the $710M HASC cut, and what the production ecosystem's app-portability ('reuse applications') and team-membership terms are; GAO's recommended unit-by-year schedule does not yet exist.

Whether any government body (C5ISR Center, Army CTO/AO, TAK Product Center) would designate a neutral DDIL/API conformance report as accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence; this is the only event that would turn G29 from a credibility asset into a business.

Project Overmatch's 2026 scope, spend and Software Armory intake terms, which are mostly classified; the Navy may be a larger or smaller software buyer than the unclassified $139.8M core line suggests.

The 2026 status of the fires chain (AFATDS/JADOCS/Joint Fires Network) and its NGC2 replacement path, GCCS-J/JPES, and cross-domain-solution procurement, all marked 'Public evidence insufficient'; these determine whether legacy-translation demand is real or already assigned.
Whether SWFT actually became a mandatory authorization route in 2026 (vendor-blog evidence only) and whether reciprocity improves, since ATO friction is the shared gate for every app-layer entrant.

Whether EU/NATO instruments (DIANA rapid adoption, EDF/EDIP control tests, Germany's D-LBO, the UK Digital Targeting Web) give an EU-domiciled company founded by the German founder a structurally larger addressable market than a U.S.-domiciled ITAR-exposed product; the study rates this INFERENCE/MEDIUM and it needs both counsel and a market test.
saturation_statement: This synthesis rests on fifteen segment deep dives, five buyer maps, seven evidence sweeps, fourteen company records and a 71-candidate to 36-entry gap registry with full red teams; it was searched through WebSearch (capped in every stage), Bigdata.com full-text indexes (GAO, af.mil, transcripts, SEC filings) and GitHub code, with WebFetch to .gov, .mil and most news domains egress-blocked throughout, and this session used four targeted WebSearch calls to re-verify GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20), the November 2025 Warfighting Acquisition System memo, the FY27 Maven/JFN request and SWFT's status. Coverage is strong for NGC2, Maven, TITAN, IBCS, DAF Battle Network, SDA transport, Replicator/DAWG, PC-C6, the TAK/CoT/Lattice data models, acquisition-reform memos and the founders' regulatory position. It is thin or absent (marked 'Public evidence insufficient') for Overmatch specifics, the fires chain (AFATDS/JADOCS/JFN), GCCS-J/JPES, the DCGS family, cross-domain-solution procurement, electromagnetic battle management, tactical logistics C2 systems, the texts of the April 2026 Maven directive and the September 2025 NGC2 security memo, DODIG-2025-126 findings, PE-level budget lines for a dozen programs, any MPE/coalition RFI (none found; not evidence of opportunity) and any independent sensor-to-shooter timing measurement. RECALL items in the corpus are labeled and were not re-verified this session; no contract numbers, dollar amounts, dates or URLs were invented, and where sources conflict (Maven program-of-record month) the conflict is stated rather than resolved.
